name: Yelamu
note: Ramaytush Ohlone tribelet of the San Francisco peninsula (160-300 people at contact per Milliken). Drawn into Mission Dolores from 1777; end year estimated = last baptism of a peninsula native at Mission Dolores (1800, NPS GOGA history ch. 4). Label anchor arbitrary (central SF).

name: El Presidio de San Francisco
note: Spanish fort founded 17 Sep 1776 (site chosen by Anza 28 Mar 1776); Mexican after 1821; reopened as a US Army post 1848.

name: Presidio
note: US Army post 1848-1994, now a national park site (Presidio Trust / GGNRA).

name: Misión San Francisco de Asís
note: Mission founded 1776 (site occupied 29 Jun, chapel dedicated 9 Oct); called Mission Dolores after the Arroyo de los Dolores. Secularization forced sale of mission lands from 1834.

name: Mission Dolores
note: Village around the secularized mission (1834 on); today the Mission Dolores sub-area of the Mission District, the city's oldest neighborhood.

name: Yerba Buena
note: Mexican pueblo on Yerba Buena Cove (authorised 1834; W. A. Richardson built the first dwelling 1835 at today's Portsmouth Square). Renamed San Francisco 30 Jan 1847.

name: San Francisco
note: Renamed from Yerba Buena by alcalde Washington Bartlett 30 Jan 1847; incorporated as a city 15 Apr 1850; city and county consolidated 1856. Label anchor at the Plaza (Portsmouth Square), seat of the town government 1849-50 and of the City Hall at 750 Kearny St from 1852; the anchor moves when the new City Hall was begun on the Civic Center site (1871; anchor year is a label convention, estimated).

name: San Francisco
note: City of San Francisco (renamed from Yerba Buena 30 Jan 1847; incorporated 15 Apr 1850; city and county consolidated 1856). Label anchor at the Civic Center from the start of the City Hall there (begun 1871, finished 1899; today's City Hall 1915); before that the label stands at Portsmouth Square (sf_san_francisco_1847).

name: Mission District
note: Grew along the Mission Plank Road (toll road from downtown to Mission Dolores, opened 1851); name from the mission.

name: Little Chile (Chilecito)
note: Chilean Gold Rush settlement bounded by Montgomery, Pacific, Jackson and Kearny Streets; "early 1850s". End year estimated.

name: Sydney Town
note: Waterfront district around Pacific & Montgomery settled by Australian "Sydney Ducks" from late 1849; by the 1860s called the Barbary Coast (end year = midpoint of 1860s, estimated).

name: Barbary Coast
note: Red-light and saloon district named by sailors in the 1860s (start = midpoint, estimated); closed down after Mayor Rolph's 1917 campaign against brothels.

name: Jackson Square
note: Surviving Gold Rush-era commercial blocks on the old Barbary Coast; Jackson Square Historic District listed on the NRHP 18 Nov 1971.

name: Happy Valley
note: Gold Rush tent city along Mission St between First and Third Sts (1849); the tents were gone by 1852 but the name stayed in use for the First St area through the 1850s-60s (end year estimated).

name: Tar Flat
note: Industrial/working-class flat between First, Mission, Folsom Sts and the bay, named for tar runoff from the gas works (1850s; start estimated). Name persisted through the late 19th c.; district burned 1906 (end estimated).

name: South Park
note: Oval park block assembled by George Gordon 1852 as an exclusive residential enclave (park built 1855).

name: South of Market
note: Named for its position south of Market Street (Gold Rush era; start estimated). Shortened to "SoMa", which took off in the 1990s.

name: South of the Slot
note: Nickname for South of Market from the cable slot in Market Street (Market St cable lines from 1883); still current in Jack London's 1909 story "South of the Slot" (end year estimated).

name: SoMa
note: Acronym for South of Market that took off with the 1990s dot-com boom (start = midpoint of 1990s, estimated).

name: Chinatown
note: Chinese quarter around Portsmouth Square and Dupont St (Grant Ave) from the Gold Rush; Mayor Geary formally welcomed Chinese residents at Portsmouth Square 28 Aug 1850 (start estimated).

name: Manilatown
note: Filipino American district around Kearny & Jackson Sts that thrived from the 1920s (start = midpoint, estimated) until the 1977 I-Hotel eviction.

name: Financial District
note: Banking district on Montgomery St ("Wall Street of the West") over the filled Yerba Buena Cove; start estimated (Gold Rush 1850s).

name: North Beach
note: Named for the beach on the north shore (Gold Rush era; filled later 19th c.); Italian "Little Italy" after 1906. Start estimated (1850s midpoint).

name: East Street
note: Waterfront street along the seawall, shown as East Street on the 1869 Britton & Rey map (start = earliest map attestation, estimated).

name: The Embarcadero
note: East Street renamed The Embarcadero by the Board of Supervisors in 1909 (street-renaming commission).

name: Fisherman's Wharf
note: First state-owned Fisherman's Wharf, built 1884 at the foot of Union St (location approximate); the fleet moved to the Taylor St site set aside by the state in 1900.

name: Fisherman's Wharf
note: The state set aside the waterfront between the foot of Taylor and Leavenworth Sts for commercial fishing boats in 1900 (today's wharf, label anchor); the first state-owned Fisherman's Wharf (1884) was at the foot of Union St.

name: Union Square
note: Plaza set aside 1850; named for the pro-Union rallies held there in 1860-61 (start estimated).

name: Tenderloin
note: Informally "the Tenderloin" from the 1890s (start = midpoint, estimated); not on maps before the 1930s (labelled "Downtown").

name: Civic Center
note: Civic Center bond issued 29 Mar 1912; City Hall begun 1913. Old City Hall (1871-1906) stood on the site.

name: Loma Alta
note: Spanish/Mexican name ("high hill"); start = Spanish settlement (estimated).

name: Telegraph Hill
note: Named for the signal semaphore erected Sept 1849 (telegraph to Point Lobos 1853).

name: Russian Hill
note: Named in the Gold Rush era for a Russian sailors' cemetery found at the top (start estimated).

name: California Hill
note: Early name after California Street climbing its east face; start and end estimated.

name: Nob Hill
note: Renamed for the railroad "nobs" (Big Four) who built mansions there in the 1870s (start estimated).

name: Rincon Hill
note: Named after Rincon Point; the city's most prestigious residential hill in the 1850s-60s; cut down by the 1869 Second St Cut and the 1930s Bay Bridge approach. Start estimated.

name: Los Pechos de la Chola
note: Spanish-era name for the twin summits; start = Spanish settlement (estimated).

name: Twin Peaks
note: Renamed under American control (start estimated = 1848 cession).

name: Mount Davidson
note: Formerly Blue Mountain; renamed 1911 for surveyor George Davidson at the urging of the Sierra Club. Highest point in SF.

name: El Divisadero
note: Spanish name for Lone Mountain ("lookout point"; origin of Divisadero St). Start = Spanish settlement (estimated).

name: Lone Mountain
note: Name in use by 30 May 1854 when Lone Mountain Cemetery opened at its foot.

name: Lone Mountain Cemetery
note: Opened 30 May 1854; renamed Laurel Hill Cemetery 1867.

name: Laurel Hill Cemetery
note: Renamed 1867; graves moved to Colma from 1940, all remains removed by 1941.

name: Laurel Heights
note: Built on the former Laurel Hill Cemetery after the graves were removed (1940s); start estimated (post-war subdivision).

name: Mount Sutro
note: Originally Mount Parnassus (Adolph Sutro's name); renamed for Sutro after his death (1898). Start estimated.

name: Potrero Nuevo
note: Mission pasture ("new pasture") named by Spanish missionaries in the late 1700s; granted to the de Haro twins 1844. Start estimated.

name: Potrero Hill
note: Working-class neighborhood from the 1850s (start = midpoint, estimated).

name: Corona Heights
note: Former quarry hill (Gray Bros. from 1899) bought by the city and officially named Corona Heights in 1941.

name: Western Addition
note: Area west of Larkin St platted under the 1855 Van Ness Ordinance (aldermen appointed 1855 to lay out and name its streets).

name: Hayes Valley
note: After Hayes St / landholder Thomas Hayes; streets named by an 1856 committee (start estimated).

name: Alamo Square
note: Park around a watering hole created 1856 by Mayor Van Ness; Victorians spared by 1906 fire and 1960s redevelopment.

name: Fillmore
note: Fillmore Street became a temporary downtown after the 1906 earthquake; district named after the street.

name: Harlem of the West
note: Jazz-era nickname of the Fillmore in the 1940s-50s (start = midpoint of 1940s, estimated); ended by the A-2 redevelopment project begun 1966.

name: Japantown (Nihonjin-machi)
note: Japanese community moved to the Western Addition after 1906; emptied by forced removal and incarceration in 1942.

name: Japantown
note: Japanese Americans returned from 1945 after the exclusion order was lifted; Japan Center opened 1968.

name: Pacific Heights
note: First developed in the 1870s (start = midpoint, estimated).

name: Cow Hollow
note: Named for the dairies around Washerwoman's Lagoon (earlier "Spring Valley"); livestock ordered out 1891. Start estimated.

name: Harbor View
note: Shore district named after the Harbor View Baths resort opened 1864 near Jefferson & Baker Sts; filled for the exposition from 1912 (end estimated).

name: Panama-Pacific International Exposition
note: Exposition grounds on filled Harbor View flats; fair open 20 Feb-4 Dec 1915; buildings razed afterwards except the Palace of Fine Arts.

name: Marina District
note: Exposition land sold and subdivided after 1915; built out in the 1920s; named for the municipal marina (start estimated).

name: Black Point
note: Spanish Punta de San José / Punta Medanos; called Black Point after 1849 for its dark bay laurels.

name: Fort Mason
note: Defenses named for Richard Barnes Mason in 1882.

name: Presidio Terrace
note: First master-planned residence park on the West Side; construction began 1905.

name: Jordan Park
note: Residence park established 1906.

name: Sea Cliff
note: Residence park established 1913 (Spanish-era name of the area: Coyote Gulch).

name: Outside Lands
note: 19th-c. name for the dunes of the present Richmond and Sunset; title settled by Act of Congress 8 Mar 1866. End estimated (Richmond named 1890, Sunset c. 1886).

name: Richmond District
note: Named after George Turner Marsh's "Richmond House" (1876); supervisors designated "The Richmond District" in 1890. Officially "Park-Presidio District" 1917-2009.

name: Inner Richmond
note: Eastern part of the Richmond District (SF Planning analysis neighborhood); year = parent district name (sub-area name date undocumented).

name: Outer Richmond
note: Western part of the Richmond District (SF Planning analysis neighborhood); year = parent district name (sub-area name date undocumented).

name: Sunset District
note: Name said to be coined by developer Aurelius Buckingham in 1886 (alt. from the 1894 Midwinter Fair "Sunset City"); dunes until the 1917-18 Twin Peaks Tunnel.

name: Inner Sunset
note: Northeast corner of the Sunset, first to develop after the 1894 Midwinter Fair (start estimated).

name: Outer Sunset
note: Sand dunes until the Twin Peaks Tunnel (1917); built out 1920s-40s (start estimated).

name: Parkside
note: Development announced July 1905 by a William Crocker syndicate on former Sutro land.

name: Haight-Ashbury
note: Farms and dunes until the Haight Street Cable Railroad opened 1883 (start estimated); hippie center 1966-67.

name: Cole Valley
note: Grew around the streetcar stop at the Sunset Tunnel entrance (Carl & Cole; tunnel opened 1928). Start estimated.

name: Eureka Valley
note: Part of Horner's Addition, developed from 1887 when the Market Street Railway line reached it (Eureka Valley Improvement Association 1905).

name: The Castro
note: Castro St area of Eureka Valley (named for José Castro); became the city's gay village in the 1960s-70s and the common name of the district (start estimated).

name: Horner's Addition
note: John M. Horner bought this part of Rancho San Miguel from José de Jesús Noé in 1854 and subdivided it; still the assessor's name. End estimated.

name: Noe Valley
note: Named for José de Jesús Noé, last Mexican alcalde; when the name replaced Horner's Addition is undocumented (start estimated).

name: Bernal Heights
note: Part of José Cornelio Bernal's 1839 rancho; subdivided by F. L. A. Pioche by 1860.

name: Dogpatch
note: Industrial waterfront of Potrero Point; first press uses of the name in early-1970s Chronicle stories (start estimated). Historic district 2002.

name: Mission Bay
note: Redevelopment area announced by the Board of Supervisors 1998 on the filled bay and rail yards (UCSF campus).

name: Woodward's Gardens
note: Amusement park, zoo and conservatory on two blocks bounded by Mission, Valencia, 13th and 15th Sts, 1865-1891.

name: Butchertown
note: "New Butchertown" of 100+ slaughterhouses on pilings along Islais Creek from 1871; declined after 1906, gone by the 1960s (end = midpoint, estimated).

name: Bayview
note: Name from the Bay View Park race track, attested in Mark Twain's dispatch of 10 Sep 1864; later applied to the flats south of Hunters Point (start = first attestation, estimated).

name: La Punta Concha
note: Named Punta Concha (Conch Point) in 1775 by Juan Bautista Aguirre, pilot of Ayala's San Carlos; later also "Beacon Point".

name: Hunters Point
note: Named for the Hunter family, who bought land from Bernal in 1849 and tried to sell lots for a "South San Francisco" town in 1850.

name: Hunters Point Dry Docks
note: Commercial shipyard with two graving docks established 1870 (first Pacific-coast drydock 1867); bought by the Navy 1940.

name: San Francisco Naval Shipyard
note: Navy shipyard operating from 1941 (bought 1940).

name: Hunters Point Naval Shipyard
note: Deactivated and renamed 1974; closed permanently 1994 (BRAC 1991).

name: Visitacion Valley
note: Valley named in Rancho Cañada de Guadalupe la Visitación y Rodeo Viejo (Jacob Leese took possession 1838, title 1841).

name: Little Hollywood
note: Developed by the Crocker Estate Co. in the early 1920s as the "Bayshore Tract" (nickname date undocumented; start estimated).

name: Excelsior
note: Excelsior Homestead filed at City Hall 15 Apr 1869.

name: Crocker-Amazon
note: Crocker Estate Company's Crocker-Amazon Tract, developed in earnest after 1912 (start estimated).

name: Portola
note: Settled after 1906 by Jewish and Italian nurserymen ("Garden District"); named after the Portola School (start estimated).

name: Outer Mission
note: Developed around the 1910s as an extension of the Mission (start = midpoint, estimated).

name: Glen Park
note: First use of the name with A. S. Baldwin's Glen Park Company (zoo/pleasure ground) in 1897; streets mapped 1872.

name: Sunnyside
note: Sunnyside Land Company (pres. Behrend Joost) laid out the tract and advertised it April 1891.

name: Ingleside
note: Named for the Ingleside Inn roadhouse; Ingleside Racetrack opened 28 Nov 1895 (start = racetrack, estimated).

name: Ingleside Terraces
note: Residence park on the former Ingleside Racetrack, established 1911.

name: Oceanview
note: Railroad station area of the SF & San Jose RR; established as a community in the 1910s (start = midpoint, estimated).

name: Forest Hill
note: Residence park; development began 1912.

name: St. Francis Wood
note: Residence park established 1912.

name: Balboa Terrace
note: Residence park established 1920.

name: Westwood Park
note: Developed by Baldwin & Howell from 1916; built 1918-1923.

name: Westwood Highlands
note: Subdivision of 283 homes built 1925-1929.

name: Miraloma Park
note: Tract opened by Meyer Brothers in 1926; built 1926-1950s.

name: Sherwood Forest
note: Built beginning in the 1940s on large lots on Mount Davidson's SW slope (start = midpoint, estimated).

name: West Portal
note: Named for the western portal of the Twin Peaks Tunnel (streetcar service 1918).

name: Parkmerced
note: MetLife garden-apartment development designed early 1940s; first tenants early 1944; completed early 1950s.

name: Midtown Terrace
note: 150-acre tract for 800 homes announced 1954 (Standard Building Co.); built late 1950s.

name: Diamond Heights
note: Redevelopment Agency project (1948-1978); final plan approved 24 Oct 1955.

name: Treasure Island
note: Artificial island built 1936-37 for the 1939 Golden Gate International Exposition; Naval Station 1941-1997; now a neighborhood.

name: Golden Gate International Exposition
note: World's fair on Treasure Island, seasons 1939 and 1940.

name: Chutes at the Beach
note: Amusement area by Ocean Beach (concessions from c. 1913) named Chutes at the Beach by 1921.

name: Playland-at-the-Beach
note: Renamed Playland-at-the-Beach by George Whitney (1928; some say 1926); closed Labor Day 1972 and torn down 4 Sep 1972.

name: Yerba Buena Cove
note: Anchorage below the later Yerba Buena (name first recorded by Vancouver, 1792); filled between the Gold Rush and 1860.

name: Mission Bay
note: Tidal bay and marsh south of Rincon Point (start estimated); cut off by the Long Bridge (1864-65) and filled c. 1860-1910, finished with 1906 rubble.

name: Islais Creek
note: Named for islay (holly-leaf cherry); "Los Islais" first appears on Mexican maps in 1834.

name: Arroyo de los Dolores
note: Arroyo de Nuestra Señora de los Dolores, the creek that gave Mission Dolores its name (1776). End estimated.

name: Mission Creek
note: English name of the creek (start estimated); culverted except the channel by China Basin. Label at the surviving channel.

name: Lake Merced
note: Christened Laguna de Nuestra Señora de la Merced by Bruno de Heceta's party in 1775; recorded by Font on the Anza expedition, March 1776.

name: Castillo de San Joaquín
note: Spanish adobe battery on Punta del Cantil Blanco built 1794; levelled for Fort Point (begun 1853).

name: Fort Point
note: Brick fort built 1853-1861 on the site of the Castillo.

name: Isla de los Alcatraces
note: Ayala's 1775 chart name for today's Yerba Buena Island; Beechey's survey of the bay (HMS Blossom, 1826) moved the name Alcatraz to the present Alcatraz Island. End year = Beechey's survey (estimated).

name: Yerba Buena Island
note: Yerba Buena Island after the name Alcatraces moved to the rock to the west (Beechey's 1826 survey; start estimated); official name in the 1850 county-boundary act; "Goat Island" (for Nye's goats) in widespread popular use.

name: Goat Island
note: US Board on Geographic Names adopted Goat Island in 1895.

name: Yerba Buena Island
note: Changed back to Yerba Buena Island 3 Jun 1931.

name: Alcatraz Island
note: Ayala's 1775 "Isla de los Alcatraces" was today's Yerba Buena Island; the name was applied to this rock by Capt. Frederick W. Beechey's survey of 1826 (start estimated; Duhaut-Cilly calls it Alcatraz in Aug 1827); fort 1850s, federal prison 1934-63.

name: Boca del Puerto de San Francisco
note: Spanish name of the strait; Ayala first sailed through 5 Aug 1775 (start).

name: Golden Gate
note: Named "Chrysopylae" / Golden Gate by John C. Frémont, 1 Jul 1846.

name: Point Lobos
note: Punta de Lobos ("point of the sea lions"), Spanish-era name in use by the start of the timeline (first-use date not established).

name: Ocean Beach
note: Natural feature labelled for the whole timeline; first use of the English name not established (part of the "Outside Lands" in the 19th c.).

name: Anza Vista
note: Built on the former Calvary Cemetery (graves moved to Colma 1930s-40s), redeveloped in the early 1950s with a Sears store (start estimated); named for Juan Bautista de Anza.

name: Lakeshore
note: Area north of Lake Merced developed by the Gellerts' Standard Building Co. as "Lakeshore Park" around 1940 (start estimated).

name: Candlestick Point
note: Natural feature labelled for the whole timeline; said to be named for Candlestick Rock, a pinnacle at the tide line (first use of the name not established).

name: Oakland
note: Carpentier, Adams and Moon began developing downtown on Peralta land in 1851; incorporated as a town 4 May 1852.

name: San Antonio
note: Settlement begun 1851 when James Larue bought Peralta land east of San Antonio Creek; joined Clinton as Brooklyn 1856. Label at the old San Antonio plaza / landing (today's San Antonio Park).

name: Clinton
note: Early-1850s town on the east side of the San Antonio estuary (start estimated; location approximate); merged with San Antonio as Brooklyn 1856.

name: Brooklyn
note: Formed 1856 from San Antonio and Clinton, named for the Mormon ship Brooklyn; absorbed Lynn and incorporated 1870; annexed to Oakland 1872.

name: East Oakland
note: Former Brooklyn after the 1872 annexation; later also Fruitvale, Elmhurst and other towns annexed 1909 (start estimated). Label anchor at the former Brooklyn (it previously sat on Fruitvale's label).

name: West Oakland
note: Western terminus of the transcontinental railroad from 1869; railroad workers settled the district (start estimated).

name: North Oakland
note: Annexed to Oakland 1897.

name: Temescal
note: Village around Vicente Peralta's estate, named for Temescal Creek (Nahuatl "sweat lodge"); North Temescal post office 1877.

name: Temescal
note: Part of North Oakland after the 1897 annexation.

name: Klinknerville
note: Charles Klinkner's 75-home settlement established 1885 (post office 1887); renamed Golden Gate in 1888.

name: Golden Gate
note: Klinknerville renamed Golden Gate in 1888 (listed as Golden Gate, pop. 788, in the 1890 census); annexed to Oakland 1897.

name: Golden Gate
note: Oakland neighborhood after the 1897 annexation (the town was renamed from Klinknerville to Golden Gate in 1888).

name: Fruitvale
note: Named after Henderson Luelling's 1854 "Fruit Vale" nursery; unincorporated town annexed to Oakland by 1909.

name: Fruitvale
note: Oakland neighborhood after annexation (1909).

name: Elmhurst
note: Railroad station "Jones" renamed Elmhurst 1869; post office 1892; annexed to Oakland 1909.

name: Elmhurst
note: East Oakland neighborhood after the 1909 annexation.

name: Dimond
note: Named for Hugh Dimond, who bought the land in 1867; Dimond post office 1891.

name: Prescott
note: West Oakland neighborhood founded 1869, named for historian William H. Prescott.

name: Glenview
note: Subdivided around 1910 by Wickham Havens Inc. (start estimated).

name: Trestle Glen
note: Named for a railroad trestle built 1893 (removed 1906).

name: Jack London Square
note: Waterfront area between Broadway, Webster, the Embarcadero and the estuary named Jack London Square in 1951.

name: Lake Merritt
note: Tidal lagoon of the San Antonio estuary dammed under mayor Samuel Merritt (1867-69) and named for him (start estimated).

name: Lake Temescal
note: Reservoir created by damming Temescal Creek in 1868; regional park 1936.

name: Ocean View
note: Stagecoach-stop settlement on the bay shore (start estimated: early 1850s; Ocean View School 1856); included in Berkeley's 1878 incorporation.

name: West Berkeley
note: Name of former Ocean View after Berkeley incorporated in 1878.

name: Berkeley
note: Named in 1866 by College of California trustees (after Bishop George Berkeley); incorporated 4 Apr 1878 together with Ocean View.

name: Lorin
note: Settlement at the Berkeley Branch railroad stop at Adeline & Alcatraz (branch opened 1876; start estimated); voted to annex to Berkeley 1892.

name: Lorin
note: South Berkeley district after annexation.

name: Southside
note: Grew after the University of California moved to Berkeley in 1873 (start estimated).

name: Elmwood
note: Rural estates subdivided in the housing boom after the 1906 earthquake (start estimated).

name: Thousand Oaks
note: First subdivided 1909 (and 1917).

name: Ocean View
note: Incorporated 22 Sep 1908 as the City of Ocean View; renamed Albany by voters in 1909.

name: Albany
note: Renamed 1909 to distinguish it from Berkeley's Ocean View district.

name: Emeryville
note: Joseph S. Emery bought and subdivided Peralta plot 6 in 1859 (the settlement was known as Emery's); name Emeryville first documented with the post office of 1884 (label start); incorporated 2 Dec 1896.

name: Piedmont
note: Name introduced by James Gamble's Piedmont Land Company, founded 1877; incorporated 1907.

name: Encinal de San Antonio
note: Oak-covered peninsula (Spanish "Encinal") of Rancho San Antonio; start = 1820 Peralta grant (estimated).

name: Alameda
note: Founded 6 Jun 1853 (village at Encinal & High Sts); incorporated 19 Apr 1854; Woodstock and the whole island included 1872. Label at Park St / City Hall, the town centre since the 1870s.

name: San Leandro
note: Townsite laid out from 1855 by Estudillo's sons-in-law on Rancho San Leandro; county seat 1856-72; incorporated 1872.

name: Squattersville
note: Original 1851 name of San Lorenzo; renamed by 1854 (post office).

name: San Lorenzo
note: Post office opened 1854; on former Rancho San Lorenzo.

name: Haywards
note: Named for William Hayward's hotel (1852); post office "Haywood" 1860; chartered as the town of Haywards 1876.

name: Hayward
note: Officially renamed Hayward (dropping the "s") 1911.

name: Mount Eden
note: Founded 1850 by farmers from Mount Eden, Kentucky; mostly annexed by Hayward.

name: Russell City
note: Named 1853 after Joel Russell; Black and Latino community annexed by Hayward 1964, residents evicted and town razed for industry.

name: Union City
note: Founded 1850 by John and William Horner, named for their steamer "The Union"; merged with New Haven as Alvarado.

name: New Haven
note: Town founded 1851 next to Union City; merged into Alvarado (location approximate).

name: Alvarado
note: Named for Governor Juan Alvarado; first Alameda County seat 1853 (Union City article gives 1854 for the merger); incorporated with Decoto as Union City 1959.

name: Decoto
note: Railroad town on Ezra Decoto's land (sold 1867), founded 1870; part of Union City 1959.

name: Union City
note: Incorporated 26 Jan 1959 from Alvarado and Decoto, reviving the 1850 name.

name: Newark
note: Washington Township land subdivided by the Pacific Land Investment Co. in 1878 to form the town; incorporated 1955. Label at the old town by the railroad (Thornton Ave / Sycamore St).

name: Misión San José
note: Mission founded 11 Jun 1797 by Fermín Lasuén; closed as an agricultural commune in the mid-1830s after secularization (end estimated).

name: Mission San Jose
note: Town around the former mission; one of five towns merged as Fremont 23 Jan 1956, name survives as a district.

name: Washington Township
note: Alameda County township formed 1853 (Mission San José, Centerville, Niles, Irvington, Warm Springs, Alvarado, Newark, Decoto).

name: Fremont
note: Incorporated 23 Jan 1956 from Mission San José, Centerville, Niles, Irvington and Warm Springs; named for John C. Frémont.

name: Centerville
note: Washington Township town (start estimated, 1850s); merged into Fremont 1956, now a district.

name: Niles
note: Railroad town at Vallejo's Mills at the mouth of Niles Canyon (start estimated, transcontinental line 1869); merged into Fremont 1956.

name: Washington Corners
note: Crossroads settlement; post office Washington Corners established at Washington College in 1870 and so named on the 1878 county map; renamed Irving 1884.

name: Irvington
note: Washington Corners renamed Irving in 1884 (after Judge Irving), Irvington after the railroad's timetable spelling; merged into Fremont 1956. Label at Irvington Square (Five Corners).

name: Warm Springs
note: Named for the hot springs on Rancho Agua Caliente (start estimated); merged into Fremont 1956.

name: Sunol
note: Post office opened 1871 (briefly "Sunolglen"); named for Antonio Suñol.

name: Laddsville
note: First valley settlement around Alphonso Ladd's 1860s hotel (start = midpoint, estimated); superseded by Mendenhall's Livermore townsite 1869.

name: Livermore
note: William Mendenhall set aside 100 acres for the townsite in 1869, named for Robert Livermore; incorporated 1876.

name: Alisal
note: Earlier settlement around the Alviso adobe "El Alisal" (the sycamores) on Rancho Santa Rita (dates estimated).

name: Pleasanton
note: Named by John Kottinger for Gen. Alfred Pleasonton; established 1869, incorporated 1894.

name: Dublin
note: Irish settlers bought land from José María Amador and founded a town in 1850 (earlier Alamilla Springs); incorporated 1982.

name: Cherryland
note: Farm subdivision named Cherryland initiated 1911.

name: Martinez
note: Laid out 1849, named for Ygnacio Martínez of Rancho El Pinole; county seat 1850; incorporated 1876.

name: Smith's Landing
note: Settlement of the Smith brothers (1849) near Marsh's 1848 landing on the San Joaquin.

name: Antioch
note: Renamed Antioch at the town picnic 4 Jul 1851; incorporated 1872.

name: New York of the Pacific
note: Town laid out 1849 by Col. Jonathan D. Stevenson on Rancho Los Médanos; coal port after 1859 (end estimated).

name: Black Diamond
note: Coal landing ("Black Diamond Landing") for the Nortonville mines from 1859; renamed Pittsburg 1911 (start estimated).

name: Pittsburg
note: Renamed Pittsburg in 1911; city incorporated 1903.

name: Nortonville
note: Coal town founded 1861 by Noah Norton; mines closed after the 1882 peak and the town was soon deserted (end estimated).

name: Somersville
note: Black Diamond coal town; post office 1863-1910.

name: Concord
note: Founded 1869 as Todos Santos by Salvio Pacheco II, name soon changed to Concord; incorporated 1905.

name: Pacheco
note: Laid out 1857 and named for Salvio Pacheco.

name: The Corners
note: Crossroads settlement begun by William Slusher 1849 on "Nuts Creek"; Walnut Creek House hotel 1855.

name: Walnut Creek
note: Post office named Walnut Creek Dec 1862; incorporated 1914. Label at the old crossroads (Main St / Mt. Diablo Blvd).

name: Acalanes
note: Elam Brown's settlement on Rancho Acalanes (1848); "Acalanus" post office 1854.

name: Lafayette
note: Town founded/renamed Lafayette 1857; incorporated 1968. Label at the Plaza (Mt. Diablo Blvd / Moraga Rd).

name: Orinda Park
note: Orinda Park post office opened 1888.

name: Orinda
note: Post office renamed Orinda 1895; incorporated 1985.

name: Moraga
note: On the 1835 Rancho Laguna de los Palos Colorados of Joaquín Moraga; first post office 1886; incorporated 1974.

name: Alamo
note: John Jones became first postmaster 1852.

name: Danville
note: Danville post office opened 1860; incorporated 1982.

name: San Ramon
note: Official place name from the permanent post office of 1873 (settled 1850 on Amador's Rancho San Ramon); incorporated 1983.

name: Clayton
note: Laid out 1857 by Joel Clayton at the foot of Mount Diablo; incorporated 1964.

name: Pleasant Hill
note: Post-war suburb, no post office until 1948; incorporated 1961.

name: Brentwood
note: Laid out on John Marsh's former Rancho Los Méganos; first post office 1878; incorporated 1948.

name: Oakley
note: First post office 1898; incorporated 1999.

name: Byron
note: First post office 1878.

name: Knightsen
note: Founded 1898 ahead of the Santa Fe Railway line.

name: Discovery Bay
note: Planned community begun 1964 on the Byron Tract.

name: Bay Point
note: Town platted by the Bay Point Land Co.; settlement began 26 Nov 1907.

name: Port Chicago
note: Renamed 1931 (post office Bay Point 1897-1931, Port Chicago 1931-1969); site of the 1944 explosion; the town ceased to exist in 1969, bought out for the Concord Naval Weapons Station buffer.

name: Clyde
note: Company town built 1917 for Pacific Coast Shipbuilding workers.

name: Bay Point
note: Renamed from West Pittsburg by election in 1993, reviving the historical name of the area.

name: Port Costa
note: Founded 1879 as the landing for the Central Pacific's train ferry Solano.

name: Crockett
note: Thomas Edwards built the first home in 1867 on land bought from Judge J. B. Crockett; name first documented with the post office "Crocketville" of 1883, renamed Crockett the same year (label start).

name: Rodeo
note: Stockyard town laid out on land sold by Patrick Tormey in 1890; post office 1892.

name: Hercules
note: Company town of the Hercules Powder Co. (incorporated 1882); city incorporated Dec 1900.

name: Pinole
note: On Rancho El Pinole (1823); post office when the railroad arrived 1878; incorporated 1903.

name: San Pablo
note: On Rancho San Pablo (1823); post office 1854; incorporated 1948.

name: Oak Grove
note: Called "Oak Grove" by industrial concerns from 1887 when a railroad spur reached the area.

name: El Sobrante
note: Name El Sobrante (from Rancho El Sobrante) adopted with the post office in 1941.

name: Stege
note: Founded 1876; post office 1889-1935; absorbed by Richmond and El Cerrito (end = post office closure).

name: Richmond
note: Named from the survey names Point Richmond / Richmond; post office 1900; incorporated 3 Aug 1905.

name: Rust
note: 1906 earthquake refugee camp; post office 1909 named Rust after Wilhelm Rust.

name: El Cerrito
note: Incorporated 23 Aug 1917 as El Cerrito ("little hill", for Albany Hill).

name: Kensington
note: Surveyed and named in 1911 by Robert Brousefield after London's Kensington.

name: Ompuromo
note: Yelamu/Ramaytush village southwest of Lake Merced. Location approximate. End year estimated (people drawn into Mission Dolores by c. 1800).

name: Urebure
note: Ramaytush Ohlone local tribe of the San Bruno Creek area (not a village: its village Siplichiquin is drawn and labelled from data/tables/early_region.csv). Label anchor approximate. End year estimated = the village emptied into Mission Dolores by 1785 (early_region.csv ohl_siplichiquin).

name: San Pedro y San Pablo Asistencia
note: Mission Dolores farming outpost built 1786 at the village of Pruristac; abandoned c. 1793 (site of the later Sánchez Adobe). Label at the outstation's buildings (Sánchez Adobe site), as drawn from data/tables/early_region.csv.

name: Top of the Hill
note: Refugee settlement on John Daly's dairy ranch after the 1906 earthquake (Daly City's "Top of the Hill").

name: Daly City
note: Incorporated 22 Mar 1911, named for landowner John Daly (1908 attempt as "Vista Grande"). Label at the Top of the Hill (Mission St), the town of 1911.

name: School House Station
note: Name of the post office here in 1869 ("Station"). Label at the old village by the railroad station (San Pedro Rd / Mission Rd), location approximate.

name: Colma
note: Called Colma from 1872; cemetery district after SF banned burials (1900s). Label at the old village by the railroad station (San Pedro Rd / Mission Rd), location approximate.

name: Lawndale
note: Necropolis incorporated as the Town of Lawndale 5 Aug 1924.

name: Colma
note: Renamed back to Colma in 1941 (another Lawndale existed in LA County).

name: Visitacion City
note: Platted 1908 beside the new Bayshore Cutoff railroad; later renamed Brisbane (end estimated).

name: Brisbane
note: Renamed from Visitacion City (start estimated; "City of Stars" tradition from 1939); incorporated 27 Nov 1961. Label at the town (Visitacion Ave).

name: Baden
note: Town founded by Charles Lux near the 12-Mile House after 1856; now a neighborhood of South San Francisco.

name: South San Francisco
note: Industrial city planned 1888 by G. F. Swift's meatpacking syndicate; incorporated 19 Sep 1908. Label at Grand Ave, the 1891 townsite.

name: San Bruno
note: Began as a stage stop (Thorp's Place / Clark's Station, inn 1849); post office San Bruno 1875; incorporated 1914.

name: Millbrae
note: Darius Ogden Mills bought part of Rancho Buri Buri for his estate in the 1860s (start = midpoint, estimated); incorporated 1948. Label at the old town by the station (El Camino Real).

name: Burlingame
note: Land named 1868 by William Ralston for Anson Burlingame; incorporated 1908. Label at the station / Burlingame Ave.

name: Hillsborough
note: Estate district on Rancho San Mateo (named after Hillsborough, NH, home of W. D. M. Howard's family); incorporated 5 May 1910.

name: San Mateo
note: Name from the 1770s mission outpost ("San Matheo"); stage station 1858 (start estimated); incorporated 1894. Label at downtown (B St / Third Ave) by the station.

name: San Mateo Point
note: Name on maps before 1895 (start estimated); then an island joined to the shore by marsh.

name: Coyote Point
note: Name in use from 1895 on.

name: Belmont
note: Named for a nearby hill ("bel monte") on Rancho de las Pulgas; settled 1850s (start estimated); incorporated 1926. Label at Ralston Ave / El Camino Real (station), the old village.

name: San Carlos
note: San Carlos station added 1888 on the 1863 Peninsula railroad; incorporated 1925. Label at the 1888 station.

name: Mezesville
note: Embarcadero townsite laid out 1854 by Simon Mezes on Arguello land.

name: Redwood City
note: Popular name of the lumber port; county seat from the April 1857 election (Britannica dates the name to 1867); incorporated 11 May 1867. Label at the old embarcadero town (Broadway / Main St, Courthouse Square).

name: Fair Oaks
note: Known as Fair Oaks during the 1860s (start = midpoint, estimated).

name: Atherton
note: Fair Oaks owners incorporated separately 12 Sep 1923 and took the name Atherton (Fair Oaks was taken).

name: Menlo Park
note: Dennis Oliver and D. C. McGlynn bought the land in 1851 and in August 1854 put up a gate inscribed "Menlo Park" (after Menlough, Galway) - label start; railroad station 1863; incorporated 1874-76, again 1927.

name: Ravenswood
note: Shipping-town scheme at today's Cooley Landing named Ravenswood by Isaiah Woods in 1849; it failed and Woods sold the wharf to Lester Cooley in 1868 (the name survives in the Ravenswood school district).

name: Cooley's Landing
note: Lester Cooley bought Woods' wharf in 1868; brick works until 1884, then ranch land. End year = start of the Runnymede colony (estimated).

name: Runnymede
note: Charles Weeks' poultry colony of one-acre farms ("One Acre and Independence"), from 1916; merged with Ravenswood under the name East Palo Alto in 1925. Label on Runnymede St (location approximate).

name: East Palo Alto
note: Name chosen by a vote of the residents of Runnymede and Ravenswood in 1925; unincorporated until 1 Jul 1983.

name: Woodside
note: Mathias Parkhurst bought timberland and named it "Woodside" in 1849; incorporated 1956.

name: Searsville
note: Lumber town named for John H. Sears (by 1854); bought by Spring Valley Water Works 1887 and flooded by Searsville Dam (1892).

name: Portola Valley
note: Named for Gaspar de Portolá; incorporated 14 Jul 1964 (earlier use of the name not dated here).

name: La Honda
note: J. H. Sears settled here 1862 after leaving Searsville; post office La Honda 1880.

name: San Gregorio
note: Stagecoach resort town booming in the 1850s (start = midpoint, estimated).

name: Pescadero
note: On Rancho Pescadero, granted to Juan José González in 1833 (town grew later; start = grant).

name: Spanishtown
note: Founded in the 1840s as San Benito, later called Spanishtown (start = midpoint, estimated).

name: Half Moon Bay
note: Renamed Half Moon Bay in 1874; incorporated 1959. Label at Main St.

name: El Granada
note: Planned as "Granada" on the Ocean Shore Railroad; post office recorded the name as El Granada in 1909.

name: Princeton-by-the-Sea
note: Resort/harbor village since the early 1900s (Princeton Inn) (start estimated).

name: Moss Beach
note: Resort begun with Juergen Wienke's hotel of 1881.

name: Montara
note: US Coast Survey used the name Montara in 1869 (Whitney Survey "Montoro" 1867); lighthouse 1875.

name: Pacifica
note: Incorporated 22 Nov 1957 from nine communities: Fairmont, Westview, Pacific Manor, Sharp Park, Fairway Park, Vallemar, Rockaway Beach, Linda Mar and Pedro Point.

name: Rockaway Beach
note: Coastal settlement; Rockaway Beach quarry established 1907 (start estimated); part of Pacifica 1957.

name: Foster City
note: Planned city on filled Brewer Island; first residents 7 Mar 1964; incorporated 27 Apr 1971.

name: Emerald Lake Hills
note: Two subdivisions (Emerald Lake, Emerald Hills) created around 1920 (estimated).

name: Pueblo de San José de Guadalupe
note: Founded 29 Nov 1777 at its first site by the Guadalupe River, about a mile north of today's downtown; flooded, moved south from 1791 (first-site houses in data/tables/early_region.csv stand until 1797).

name: Pueblo de San José de Guadalupe
note: Founded 29 Nov 1777, the first civil town in the Californias; this is the second site around the Pueblo Plaza (move begun 1791 because of floods, complete by 1797).

name: San Jose
note: Incorporated 27 Mar 1850 as California's first city and first state capital (1849-51).

name: Misión Santa Clara de Asís
note: Founded 12 Jan 1777 at its first site on the Guadalupe River (So-co-is-u-ka); flooded 1779 and moved (site as drawn from data/tables/early_region.csv scl_m1; location approximate).

name: Misión Santa Clara de Asís
note: Second, temporary site 1779-1784 (as drawn from data/tables/early_region.csv scl_m2; location approximate); the third church was dedicated in 1784.

name: Misión Santa Clara de Asís
note: Third (1784-1818), temporary fourth and fifth (1825) sites of the mission, all within ~400 m of the label at the present church; secularized after 1833, Native neophytes "freed" by 1836.

name: Santa Clara
note: Town around the former mission; Santa Clara College 1851; incorporated as a town 5 Jul 1852. Label at the old town beside the mission (Franklin St).

name: Alviso
note: Port of San José, chartered as a city 26 Mar 1852; consolidated with San Jose 12 Mar 1968.

name: Alviso
note: San Jose's waterfront district after the 1968 consolidation.

name: Drawbridge
note: Created 1876 by the South Pacific Coast Railroad on Station Island; hunting resort; abandoned by 1975 (ghost town).

name: New Almaden
note: Quicksilver (mercury) mine identified 1845 by Andrés Castillero; company town. Label at the Hacienda village (Casa Grande).

name: Willow Glen
note: Farming community (Willow Glen School 1863); incorporated as a city 1927; voted to join San Jose 1936.

name: Willow Glen
note: San Jose neighborhood after the 1936 annexation.

name: Naglee Park
note: General Naglee's estate subdivided 1902.

name: Heinlenville
note: San Jose Chinatown built 1887 by John Heinlen on the block bounded by 6th, 7th, Taylor and Jackson Sts (end estimated).

name: Japantown
note: Grew from Japanese boardinghouses just west of Heinlenville (start estimated, 1890s); one of three remaining US Japantowns.

name: Rose Garden
note: Named for the Municipal Rose Garden; John Crummey subdivided his orchard here in 1937 (start estimated).

name: Santa Teresa
note: Rancho Santa Teresa granted 1834 to José Joaquín Bernal (settled 1826); today a south San Jose neighborhood.

name: Milpitas
note: Name from Rancho Milpitas (1835); American farm town from the 1850s (start = midpoint, estimated); incorporated 26 Jan 1954. Label at Main St, the old town.

name: Murphy's Station
note: Railroad stop on Martin Murphy Jr.'s Bay View ranch, established 1861.

name: Encinal
note: Post office named Encinal in F. E. Cornell's store, Dec 1897.

name: Sunnyvale
note: Name adopted 24 Mar 1901 when "Encinal" and "Murphy" were refused by the Post Office; incorporated 24 Dec 1912. Label at the station / Murphy Ave.

name: Mountain View
note: Stagecoach station settled 1852, named for its view of the Santa Cruz Mountains; incorporated 7 Nov 1902. Label at Castro St, the town that grew around the 1864 railroad station (the 1852 stage stop, Old Mountain View, was on El Camino Real about 1.5 km to the south-east).

name: Mayfield
note: Town begun 1853 near Elisha Crosby's Mayfield Farm; annexed by Palo Alto 1925. Label at California Ave (Mayfield's Lincoln St).

name: College Terrace
note: Original "Palo Alto" tract, annexed by Mayfield 1891 and with it by Palo Alto 1925.

name: University Park
note: Temperance town on 740 acres bought by Timothy Hopkins in 1887 for Stanford's university.

name: Palo Alto
note: University Park incorporated as Palo Alto 16 Apr 1894 (the name had been used for College Terrace).

name: Stanford
note: Campus community of Stanford University (opened 1891).

name: Los Altos
note: Developed by Paul Shoup's Altos Land Company, formed 1906; incorporated 1 Dec 1952. Label at Main St / State St by the 1908 station.

name: Los Altos Hills
note: Incorporated 27 Jan 1956.

name: Cupertino
note: Named for Arroyo de San José de Cupertino (Anza expedition); displaced the regional name "West Side" after 1900 (start estimated); incorporated 1955.

name: Campbell
note: Benjamin Campbell's "Campbell's Place"; first subdivision recorded by 1887; incorporated 1952. Label at Campbell Ave by the station.

name: McCarthysville
note: Founded 1851 by Martin McCarthy at a toll road to the valley.

name: Bank Mills
note: Renamed Bank Mills in 1863.

name: Saratoga
note: Final name Saratoga (after Saratoga Springs, NY) 1865; incorporated 1956. Label at Saratoga Village (Big Basin Way).

name: Los Gatos
note: Grew around Forbes Mill (mid-1850s), first named for the mill, then Los Gatos after the 1839 rancho; a town by 1868 (start estimated); incorporated 1887. Label at the old town (Main St / Santa Cruz Ave, by Forbes Mill).

name: Monte Sereno
note: Incorporated 14 May 1957.

name: Morgan Hill
note: Hiram Morgan Hill contracted C. H. Phillips to subdivide his ranch in 1892; incorporated 10 Nov 1906.

name: San Ysidro
note: Village on Rancho San Ysidro, granted to Ygnacio Ortega in 1809 (start = grant).

name: Gilroy
note: Renamed for John Gilroy when the town was incorporated (1868 per article text; infobox gives 12 Mar 1870).

name: Coyote Creek
note: Named Arroyo del Coyote by Pedro Font on the Anza expedition, 31 Mar 1776.

name: Guadalupe River
note: Named Río de Nuestra Señora de Guadalupe by the Anza expedition, 30 Mar 1776.

name: Mount Hamilton
note: Named 1861 (Whitney Survey) for Rev. Laurentine Hamilton; Lick Observatory 1888.

name: Santa Clara Valley
note: Valley named after Mission Santa Clara (1777); "Valley of Heart's Delight" orchards until the 1960s.

name: Misión de la Exaltación de la Santa Cruz
note: Mission founded 28 Aug 1791 by Fermín Lasuén near the Uypi village of Aulintak; lands divided after the 1833 secularization act (end estimated).

name: Santa Cruz
note: Town grown from the mission settlement; incorporated as a town 1866, charter city 1876 (annexed Branciforte 1905).

name: Villa de Branciforte
note: Spanish civil town founded 1797 across the San Lorenzo River from the mission; annexed to Santa Cruz 1905.

name: Watsonville
note: Town laid out 1852 on Rancho Bolsa del Pajaro, named for Judge John Watson; incorporated 30 Mar 1868.

name: Camp Capitola
note: Seaside resort at Soquel Landing developed by Frederick Hihn from 1869 (start estimated).

name: Capitola
note: Incorporated 11 Jan 1949.

name: Scotts Valley
note: Named after Hiram Scott, who bought Rancho San Agustín in 1850; incorporated 1966.

name: Misión San Rafael Arcángel
note: Founded 14 Dec 1817 as a hospital asistencia of Mission Dolores (full mission status 1822); secularized 1834 (end estimated).

name: San Rafael
note: Town grown around the mission (founded 1817); incorporated 1874; county seat.

name: Saucelito
note: Town founded 1868 on Richardson's Rancho Saucelito (1838); post office "Saucelito" 1870.

name: Sausalito
note: Post office spelling changed to Sausalito 1887; incorporated 4 Sep 1893.

name: Mill Valley
note: Tamalpais Land & Water Co. formed 1889 to sell the Richardson/Throckmorton land and the railroad was extended; post office "Eastland" until 1904; incorporated 1900.

name: Larkspur
note: Town laid out by C. W. Wright in 1887; incorporated 1908.

name: Corte Madera
note: On Rancho Corte Madera del Presidio (1834); first post office 1878; incorporated 1916.

name: Ross
note: Named for James Ross, who bought Rancho Punta de Quentín in 1857 ("Ross Landing"); incorporated 1908.

name: Kentfield
note: Ross Landing station renamed Kent in the 1890s and Kentfield with the 1905 post office.

name: Junction
note: Railroad junction of the 1875 Sausalito-Tomales line, listed on maps as "Junction".

name: San Anselmo
note: Name San Anselmo came back into use 1883; incorporated 9 Apr 1907.

name: Fairfax
note: Named for Lord Charles Fairfax (Assembly speaker) who lived here in the 1850s; first post office 1910; incorporated 1931.

name: Novato
note: First post office 1856 on Rancho Novato (1839); incorporated 1960.

name: Tiburon
note: Terminus of the San Francisco & North Pacific Railroad; post office 1884; incorporated 1964.

name: Belvedere
note: Island (first Marin land grant to John Reed 1834) incorporated as Belvedere 1896.

name: San Quentin
note: Village of San Quentin State Prison employees (prison opened 1852, the state's oldest).

name: Marin City
note: Built from 1942 to house Marinship wartime shipyard workers.

name: Bolinas
note: First post office 1863 (Rancho Las Baulines, 1846).

name: Willow Camp
note: Tent settlement among the willows after the coast road from Sausalito was built in 1870.

name: Stinson Beach
note: Official town name from 1916 (post office), after landowners Rose and Nathan Stinson.

name: Olema
note: Post office 1859 (reopened 1864).

name: Olema Station
note: Railroad stop named Olema Station when the North Pacific Coast RR arrived in 1875.

name: Point Reyes Station
note: Point Reyes post office opened 1882.

name: Inverness
note: Named by a Scottish landowner; first post office 1897.

name: Tomales
note: "Tomalles" post office opened 1854.

name: Marshall
note: Named for four Marshall brothers who set up dairying in the 1850s (start = midpoint, estimated).

name: Nicasio
note: Hotel Nicasio and St. Mary's church 1867; post office 1871.

name: Napa
note: Founded by Nathan Coombs in 1847 on part of Rancho Entre Napa; incorporated 1872.

name: Sebastopol
note: Town named Sebastopol in 1855; renamed because Sonoma County had a Sebastopol.

name: Yountville
note: Renamed 1867 for George C. Yount; incorporated 1965.

name: St. Helena
note: Founded 1854 when Still and Walters bought land from Maria Soberanes Bale; incorporated 1876.

name: Calistoga
note: Sam Brannan's hot-springs resort (opened 1862) became a town when the railroad arrived 1868; incorporated 1886.

name: American Canyon
note: Incorporated 1 Jan 1992 (earlier unincorporated use of the name not dated here).

name: Benicia
note: Founded 19 May 1847 by Semple, Larkin and Vallejo, first named Francisca and soon renamed for Francisca Benicia Vallejo; state capital Feb 1853-Feb 1854; incorporated 1850.

name: Benicia Arsenal
note: Army post established 9 Apr 1849 (Benicia Barracks), later the Benicia Arsenal; deactivated 1963 and closed 1964.

name: Vallejo
note: Founded 1851 on Vallejo's Rancho Suscol as the state capital (legislature met 1852 and Jan 1853); incorporated 1868.

name: Isla de la Plana
note: Name given by Ayala's expedition in 1775. End estimated.

name: Mare Island
note: Mare Island (from Vallejo's mare); Navy shipyard from 1854 to 1996 (start estimated).

name: Fairfield
note: Founded 1856 by clipper captain Robert Waterman, named after Fairfield, Connecticut; incorporated 1903.

name: Suisun City
note: Established in the 1850s (start = midpoint, estimated), named for the Suisunes; incorporated 9 Oct 1868.

name: Cordelia
note: Founded 1853 by Robert Waterman; renamed Cordelia when the post office came c. 1869.

name: Vacaville
note: Township deeded 13 Dec 1851 on the Vaca-Peña grant, named for Juan Manuel Vaca; incorporated 1892.

name: Silveyville
note: Gold Rush stopover founded 1852; bypassed by the Central Pacific in 1868, its buildings moved to the depot town in 1871 (location approximate).

name: Dixon
note: Depot town on Thomas Dickson's land ("Dicksonville"); a mis-addressed 1872 shipment made the name Dixon; incorporated 1878.

name: Rio Vista
note: Founded 1858 as "Brazos del Rio" near Cache Slough; moved to higher ground after the 1861-62 floods ("New Rio Vista"); incorporated 1893.

name: Misión San Francisco Solano
note: Last Spanish-founded mission (4 Jul 1823, under Mexico); closed and converted to a parish 1834.

name: Sonoma
note: Pueblo founded by Mariano Vallejo on the mission lands in 1835; Bear Flag Revolt 1846; incorporated 1883.

name: Petaluma
note: American town grew after the Gold Rush on Vallejo's Rancho Petaluma (1834) by the Coast Miwok village Péta Lúuma (start estimated); incorporated 12 Apr 1858.

name: Santa Rosa
note: Named 1833 by Mexican colonists after St. Rose of Lima; Carrillo adobe 1830s; incorporated 1867-68.

name: Healdsburg
note: Harmon Heald laid out the town and plaza in 1857 on Rancho Sotoyome; incorporated 1867.

name: Pine Grove
note: Original name of the settlement (dates estimated: renamed in the late 1850s).

name: Sebastopol
note: Renamed in the late 1850s after a brawl likened to the siege of Sevastopol (start estimated); incorporated 1902.

name: Windsor
note: Post office established 1855; incorporated 1 Jul 1992.

name: Markleville
note: Stagecoach stop of R. B. Markle and W. J. Miller from 1856.

name: Cloverdale
note: Town laid out after J. A. Kleiser bought Markle's interest in 1859; incorporated 1872.

name: Cotati
note: Cotati Land Company (Page family) subdivided Rancho Cotate in 1892 (hexagonal plaza); incorporated 1963.

name: Rohnert Park
note: Planned city laid out from 1956-57 on the Rohnert seed farm; incorporated 28 Aug 1962.

name: Glen Ellen
note: Named after Charles Stuart's vineyard (house begun 1868), named for his wife Ellen.

name: Fort Ross
note: Russian-American Company settlement (Krepost' Ross), hub of Russian California 1812-1841.

name: Port Rumyantsev
note: Russian name for Bodega Bay (Zaliv Rumyantseva), given by Kuskov March 1812; port of the Fort Ross colony until 1841.

name: San Francisco Bay
note: Sighted by the Portolá expedition in Nov 1769; first entered by Ayala's San Carlos 5 Aug 1775.

name: San Pablo Bay
note: Named after Rancho San Pablo on its shore (article gives 1815 for the Spanish grant; Mexican grant 1823).

name: Suisun Bay
note: Named in 1811 after the Suisunes (Patwin).

name: Carquinez Strait
note: Named for the Karkin Ohlone (Spanish "los Carquines"); Spanish-era name in use by the start of the timeline (first-use date not established).

name: Richardson Bay
note: Named for William A. Richardson, grantee of Rancho Saucelito in 1838 (start estimated from the grant).

name: Alameda County
note: Formed 25 Mar 1853 from parts of Contra Costa and Santa Clara counties.

name: Contra Costa County
note: One of the original 27 counties (1850); "opposite coast" from San Francisco.

name: Marin County
note: Original county created 18 Feb 1850.

name: San Mateo County
note: Split from San Francisco County in 1856.

name: Santa Clara County
note: Original county (1850).

name: Solano County
note: Original county (1850), named for Chief Solano.

name: Sonoma County
note: Original county (1850); seat moved from Sonoma to Santa Rosa 1854.

name: Napa County
note: Original county (1850).

name: Santa Cruz County
note: Original county (1850); the act first named it Branciforte County, renamed Santa Cruz within weeks.

name: Angel Island
note: Named Isla de los Ángeles by Juan de Ayala, who anchored there in 1775.

name: Mount Tamalpais
note: From Coast Miwok támal pájiṣ ("west hill"); name first recorded 1845.

name: Point Reyes
note: Punta de los Reyes, Spanish name given in the 1600s; in use by the start of the timeline.

name: Point San Quentin
note: Point at the south end of Mission Bay, named by Spanish settlers in the 18th century (start estimated = Spanish settlement) and kept as Point San Quentin on US Coast Survey charts; shown as Potrero Point on maps by 1882. (Row formerly described the Marin point of the same name, which has no label; the coordinates were always this San Francisco point.)

name: Potrero Point
note: Name on maps by 1882 for the former Point San Quentin; centre of heavy industry (Union Iron Works, Pacific Rolling Mill, sugar refinery) by 1880; Dogpatch stands on it.

name: Farallon Islands
note: Spanish Farallones ("sea cliffs"); recorded by Drake 1579; name in use by the start of the timeline.

name: Monte del Diablo
note: By 1824 the area north of the mountain was called Monte del Diablo ("devil's thicket"); Americans applied it to the peak (end estimated).

name: Mount Diablo
note: Peak chosen 1851 as the initial point of the Mount Diablo Base and Meridian survey (start estimated).

name: San Bruno Mountain
note: Spanish-era name (after the San Bruno area); in use by the start of the timeline (first-use date not established).

name: Montara Mountain
note: Called "Montoro" by the Whitney Survey in 1867, "Montara" by the Coast Survey 1869.

name: Sweeney Ridge
note: Where Portolá's expedition first saw San Francisco Bay (Nov 1769); later name for the ridge (first-use date not established).

name: Mare Island Naval Shipyard
note: First US Navy base on the Pacific (1854); deactivated in the 1995 base-closure round (closed 1996).

name: Rancho San Antonio
note: Granted to Luis María Peralta 3 Aug 1820; covered the sites of Oakland, Berkeley, Alameda, Emeryville, Piedmont, Albany and San Leandro. End = Oakland incorporated on it 1852. End year = claim filed with the US Public Land Commission (Land Act of 1851) unless stated.

name: Rancho San Pablo
note: Granted 1823 to Francisco María Castro (reconfirmed 1834). End year = claim filed with the US Public Land Commission (Land Act of 1851) unless stated.

name: Rancho de las Pulgas
note: Spanish provisional grant 1795 to José Darío Argüello (Mexican confirmation 1835); patented 1857. End year = claim filed with the US Public Land Commission (Land Act of 1851) unless stated.

name: Rancho San Leandro
note: Granted 1842 to José Joaquín Estudillo. End year = claim filed with the US Public Land Commission (Land Act of 1851) unless stated.

name: Rancho Laguna de la Merced
note: Granted 1835 to José Antonio Galindo. End year = claim filed with the US Public Land Commission (Land Act of 1851) unless stated.

name: Rancho San Miguel
note: Granted 1845 to José de Jesús Noé (Twin Peaks to Noe and Eureka valleys). End year = claim filed with the US Public Land Commission (Land Act of 1851) unless stated.

name: Rancho Rincón de las Salinas y Potrero Viejo
note: Granted to José Cornelio Bernal (Rincón de las Salinas 1839, Potrero Viejo 1840); Bernal Heights to Bayview. End year = claim filed with the US Public Land Commission (Land Act of 1851) unless stated.
